bodyHtml:
Each plot of land is given a distinctive reference number by the Department of Local Land Records. This is known as a land survey number and serves as an official identification for the land, used in various legal, financial, and administrative processes related to property.

Due to digitalization, it is now simpler than ever to access land-based information on the websites of the government. You do not need to go to revenue offices anymore or struggle with paper to learn about your land or property.

This blog is meant to guide you through how to find the reference number of your land in different ways. Whether you are already a land owner or looking to buy property in Chennai, understanding the importance of property survey numbers and having them handy is helpful, particularly when dealing with real estate transactions in expanding metropolises such as Chennai.

What Is a Property Survey Number?

A property survey is a precise measurement and mapping of land carried out by authorized surveyors to ascertain its boundaries, dimensions, and physical characteristics. The land survey no is a distinctive number allocated to a given piece of land by the local revenue authority.

It is the official reference to that land in government documents and is utilized to identify it as distinct from other plots in the same location. It defines where your land starts and ends, and can uncover the precise size and configuration of a plot, including any structures, easements, or encroachments.

This number is vital in legal documents, property registration, taxation, and the settlement of land disputes. Survey numbers are usually needed when seeking a patta, confirming ownership, or exchanging lands in India. Each property survey number is associated with detailed land records, which may cover boundary, area, and ownership history.

Why You Might Need Your Survey Number

There are several scenarios where knowing your land’s official number is necessary. For instance, survey number details are required when registering a property under your name or transferring it to someone else. It’s also essential for updating land ownership after a sale or inheritance.

The survey number is so essential and very useful that you can check the land details with the survey number itself.

  • Property Registration: Mandatory to mention during the sale and transfer of ownership.
  • Mutation of Land Records: Needed while updating the new owner’s name in revenue records.
  • Payment of Property Tax: Utilized by panchayats and municipalities to determine dues.
  • Legal Documentation Before Purchase: Validates the ownership of the seller.
  • Documentation for a Loan is mandatory in processing a loan for the purchase of a house or land.
  • Find Land Details by Survey Number: You can access all your land details through your land survey number.

How to Verify a Survey Number Before Buying Property

Verifying the survey number before purchase ensures clear ownership and prevents legal issues.

  • Access your state's land records portal, input district, taluk, village, and seller details to match the survey number against official records, including village survey number list for rural areas.
  • Cross-check with encumbrance certificate (EC) and sale deed to confirm no discrepancies like old survey number to new survey number conversions from subdivisions.
  • Request patta or Record of Rights (ROR); compare boundaries and ownership history. This step is vital when buying plots in Chennai to avoid fraud.

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Find Your Property Survey Number Online

Identify Your State’s Land Records Portal

Each Indian state has a dedicated portal for land and property records. To find land survey number details online, search for the official land record website of your state using a search engine. Popular portals include those for Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, and Gujarat.

Here's a table listing six Indian states along with the names of their official land records portals:

State Land Records Portal Name Official Website
Tamil Nadu e-Services (Patta Chitta) eservices.tn.gov.in
Karnataka Bhoomi landrecords.karnataka.gov.in
Kerala Ente Bhoomi entebhoomi.kerala.gov.in
Telangana Maa Bhoomi maabhoomi.telangana.gov.in
Andhra Pradesh MeeBhoomi meebhoomi.ap.gov.in
Maharashtra Mahabhulekh bhulekh.mahabhumi.gov.in
Madhya Pradesh MP Bhulekh mpbhulekh.gov.in

Visit the Website and Choose the Right Option

After reaching the portal, find a section where you can see land details. It could be named "View Records," "Check Ownership," or "Record of Rights." You can also find land by survey number in these portals. Pick the link related to land or property details to find your land survey number.

Enter the Necessary Information

To search for your land survey number, you'll usually need to enter location-specific information like:

  • District
  • Taluk or Tehsil
  • Village or Ward

You might also be required to enter the owner's name, plot number, or other unique identifiers. Ensure spelling and choices correspond with official documents.

Retrieve the Land Information

To check the land survey number, you have to enter the property details associated with the information you entered. These are

  • Property limits
  • Area and type
  • Owner's name
  • Reference numbers

Transaction history, tax information, and land use categories may also be displayed on the page.

Save or Print the Information

Once you fetch the survey number online in the portal, you can download the land record in PDF or print the page. Save a copy for future reference, especially if you're dealing with legal or financial matters concerning the property.

How to Find Survey Number Using Google Maps / Bhuvan

Bhuvan, ISRO's GIS portal, maps land parcels with survey boundaries across India. Enter property coordinates or address, activate land records layer to view survey numbers, including city survey number online for urban plots and old survey number details.

Google Maps approximates locations, pin the site, then cross-reference with Bhuvan or state portals to find survey numbers precisely. Export maps for documentation.

Survey Number and Home Loan: Why Banks Need It

Banks require the survey number to identify the exact property, verify title clarity, and assess valuation during home loan approval. The survey number meaning here links to revenue records, confirming no encroachments, disputes, or liens via land details.

Submit it alongside the sale deed, EC, and patta for swift processing. It ensures the mortgage is created on undisputed land.

Alternative Ways to Find Your Survey Number

If the online process doesn’t work, there are other methods to find your survey number.

  • Check your property tax receipt. It includes the reference number for the land.
  • You can also check the sale deed, particularly the description of the boundaries of the property.
  • You can try the Encumbrance Certificate, which reflects ownership history.

If none of these work or are updated, a trip to the nearby revenue office or the Tahsildar's office will enable you to collect the plot survey number in person.

What to Do If Your Survey Number Is Wrong or Missing

If records show errors, visit the taluk or revenue office with sale deed, tax receipts, and ID to file for correction or mutation. For old survey number issues, request conversion to new survey number post-subdivision through official application.

Get survey number from village survey number list or city survey number online portals if missing; escalate to district collector if unresolved. Always retain certified copies.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

When you check the survey number online, you may not get the details correctly. This is due to errors in the information you enter. Mistakes like misspelling your name, choosing the wrong taluk, or entering inaccurate property details result in zero search results. As land records are highly sensitive, you need to carefully cross-check the information with your original documents.

  • Using unauthorized websites instead of the official state portals
  • Making spelling errors in the names of the owner, taluk, or village
  • Selecting the wrong administrative division (district/taluk/village)
  • Confusing plot number or door number with the land survey number
  • Leaving mandatory fields blank or submitting incomplete information
  • Not referring to official documents for accurate input

In conclusion, being aware of your land's official reference number is more than a mere formality—it's a vital aspect of looking after and safeguarding your property. It has a central role to play in land ownership, from legal confirmation to taxes and conflict resolution. Last but not least, you can also check land details using the survey number, which is one of the benefits of having it.

Thankfully, advancements in digital aids have simplified this formerly elaborate process. We invite you to spare a few minutes today to find your number, print a copy, and verify that your records are up to date and correct for any future purposes.
